properties.name: Hilo Airport
properties.note: The Army took over the Territory’s airport at Hilo in December 1941. Drawn as the airport’s ground of today, which is larger than the field of the war.

properties.name: Naval Air Station Hilo
properties.note: The Navy’s air station at the airport from 1943, which the Territory renamed General Lyman Field that year; returned to the Territory in 1952. Drawn as the airport’s ground of today.

properties.name: Kīlauea Military Camp
properties.note: A rest camp for soldiers on the rim of Kīlauea, opened in 1916 inside the national park and under the Army from 1921.

properties.name: Pōhakuloa Training Area
properties.note: The Army’s ground on the saddle between Mauna Loa, Mauna Kea and Hualālai, its barracks put up in 1955 when training moved inland from the wartime Waikoloa ground; much of it State land leased to the Army in 1964 to 2029. Today’s ground less Keʻāmuku.

properties.name: Bradshaw Army Airfield
properties.note: The training area’s airstrip, Runway 09/27 as the FAA charts it, built 1955–1956 and dedicated in 1957.

properties.name: Keʻāmuku Maneuver Area
properties.note: Ranch land bought from Parker Ranch in 2006 and added to Pōhakuloa (the land-use plan of 2021 gives 2014 for its use). Carved from the training area at the old boundary the 2000 sheet draws.

properties.name: Waikoloa Maneuver Area
properties.note: Parker Ranch land south of Waimea where the Marines of Camp Tarawa and the Army trained with live fire in the war; returned to the ranch in 1946. The Corps of Engineers’ former site.

properties.name: Hilo Airport
properties.note: Set aside at Keaukaha in 1928 and dedicated that February; held by the Army and the Navy in the war and named General Lyman Field in 1943, returned in 1952, extended east for jets in the 1960s. The airport’s ground of today.

properties.name: Runway 3/21
properties.note: The north-east to south-west runway, the field’s main one from the first; lengthened and paved in 1938 and again in the war.

properties.name: Runway 8/26
properties.note: Paved in the war as the east-west runway, the record of July 1944 the first read that gives it; extended east for jets in the 1960s.

properties.name: Keāhole Airport
properties.note: Built on the lava at Keāhole to replace the Kailua airstrip, dedicated on July 1, 1970.

properties.name: Runway 17/35
properties.note: The airport’s one runway, lengthened in the 1990s for wide-bodied aircraft.

properties.name: Kona Airport
properties.note: The airstrip on the shore north of Kailua, opened on July 10, 1949 and closed when Keāhole opened in 1970; now a park. Traced from the 2000 sheet.

properties.name: Suiter Field
properties.note: A landing field at ʻŪpolu Point set aside for the Army by executive order on June 25, 1927 and named Suiter Field in 1933; rebuilt by the Navy for carrier training in 1944 and the Territory’s after the war.

properties.name: Runway 7/25
properties.note: Paved when the field was finished to the CAA’s minimum in 1939; rebuilt by the Navy in 1944.

properties.name: Kamuela Airport
properties.note: Dedicated on August 30, 1953, replacing the wartime Marine strip of Bordelon Field nearby.

properties.name: Runway 4/22
properties.note: The airport’s one runway.

properties.name: Māmalahoa Highway
properties.note: The belt road from Hilo up to Kīlauea and round Kaʻū to Kona, improved from 1912 with the Territory’s bonds and completed round the island in 1933.

properties.name: Hawaiʻi Belt Road
properties.note: The new road from Hilo up the Hāmākua coast to Honokaʻa, laid largely on the roadbed and bridges of the railway the tsunami of 1946 ended, completed in April 1960.

properties.name: Hawaiʻi Belt Road
properties.note: From Honokaʻa up to Waimea, completed in September 1963.

properties.name: Queen Kaʻahumanu Highway
properties.note: Across the lava of the Kona coast from Kailua to Kawaihae, completed in March 1975.

properties.name: Saddle Road
properties.note: A gravel road the Army put across the saddle between Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa in 1943, handed to the Territory after the war and paved from 1949; rebuilt and partly moved north of the training area from 2007 to 2013.

properties.name: Hilo Railroad
properties.note: Benjamin Dillingham’s standard-gauge line from Waiākea to the Olaʻa sugar mill, its first stretch, on which service began in June 1900; reorganized as the Hawaiʻi Consolidated Railway in 1916 and given up after the tsunami of April 1946. Traced from the 1911–1930 sheets from Waiākea to the edge of the Olaʻa sheet.

properties.name: Hilo breakwater
properties.note: The breakwater across Hilo Bay from Puʻuʻeo toward Waiākea, begun in 1908, when the railway’s owners pressed for it, and completed in 1929.

properties.name: Kawaihae Harbor south breakwater
properties.note: Built with the dredging of the deep-draft harbour by the Corps of Engineers between 1957 and 1959, over the old salt pans of the village.

layer.key: kawaihae harbour breakwater “Kawaihae Harbor South Breakwater”

properties.name: Kawaihae light-draft harbor breakwater
properties.note: The breakwater of the small-boat harbour south of the main entrance, whose building began in 1970.

layer.key: kawaihae harbour breakwater “Kawaihae Light Draft Harbor Breakwater”

properties.name: Kawaihae light-draft harbor breakwater
properties.note: The breakwater of the small-boat harbour south of the main entrance, whose building began in 1970.
